metadata.title: Configure Docusaurus Theme and Site Branding

story.iWant: to customize the Docusaurus theme with proper branding and navigation
story.soThat: the blog reflects my professional identity and provides clear site structure

task.name: Configure Site Metadata
task.subtasks: - Update docusaurus.config.ts with site title, tagline, and description - Configure author information in blog/authors.yml - Set up social card metadata (og:image, twitter:card) - Configure favicon and site logo (if custom)

task.name: Customize Navigation Bar
task.subtasks: - Configure navbar items in themeConfig - Add blog link to navbar - Add GitHub repository link - Configure docs link if needed - Test navigation on mobile and desktop

task.name: Customize Footer
task.subtasks: - Configure footer links (social, contact, legal) - Add GitHub, LinkedIn, or other social profiles - Set copyright information - Ensure footer is responsive

task.name: Configure Color Scheme
task.subtasks: - Set primary color in themeConfig - Set secondary/accent colors - Test light and dark mode color schemes - Validate contrast ratios for accessibility

task.name: Validate Responsive Design
task.subtasks: - Test site on mobile viewport (375px, 768px) - Test site on desktop viewport (1024px, 1920px) - Verify color mode toggle works - Check for visual regressions

criterion.name: Site Configuration
criterion.description: The site configuration includes custom site title and tagline, updated navbar, customized footer, and configured color scheme (primary and secondary colors)

criterion.name: Navigation Structure
criterion.description: Navigation is properly structured with blog link, docs link (if using), GitHub repository link, and clean professional layout

criterion.name: Branding Elements
criterion.description: Branding elements are customized including site logo/favicon (if desired), author information, social card metadata, and professional description/tagline

criterion.name: Responsive Design
criterion.description: Theme renders correctly on mobile and desktop, color mode switching works, and no visual regressions from default theme

doc.title: Product Requirements Document
doc.snippet: PRD emphasizes professional identity and branding. Site should include custom title, tagline, author information, and social card metadata for sharing.

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Docusaurus uses TypeScript configuration (docusaurus.config.ts). Theme configuration in themeConfig section. Classic preset provides navbar, footer, color mode out of box. Supports MDX for blog posts.

doc.title: Architecture Document
doc.snippet: Docusaurus 3.6+ with Classic Preset for blog-ready theme with responsive design. TypeScript for type safety. Configuration in docusaurus.config.ts includes site metadata, theme configuration, and blog plugin options.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 1.2: Configure Docusaurus Theme and Site Branding
doc.snippet: Configure docusaurus.config.ts themeConfig section. Update navbar items, footer links, and color mode settings. Configure metadata for SEO (title, description, og:image). Test responsive design on mobile and desktop.

artifact.reason: Main Docusaurus configuration file - contains site metadata, theme config, navbar, footer. Needs customization for branding and navigation (lines 8-9 title/tagline, 71-147 themeConfig).
Author metadata file - currently has default Docusaurus authors. Needs replacement with James Crowley's information including name, title, socials, and image.
Custom CSS file defining color scheme. Primary colors defined in :root (light mode) and [data-theme='dark'] (dark mode). Needs customization for brand colors.
Project dependencies showing Docusaurus 3.9.2, React 19, and required packages. No changes needed but provides context for available Docusaurus features.

constraints.constraint: Use Docusaurus Classic Preset - already configured, no custom theme installation needed
TypeScript configuration format required for docusaurus.config.ts
Must maintain GitHub Pages deployment compatibility (url, baseUrl, organizationName, projectName)
Color mode must support both light and dark themes with respectPrefersColorScheme enabled
Navbar and footer must maintain responsive design for mobile and desktop
Do not remove or break existing blog functionality (RSS feeds, reading time, etc.)
Logo/favicon customization is optional - can use defaults or customize as desired
Professional tone and branding consistent with technical blog identity

interface.name: Docusaurus Config ThemeConfig
interface.signature: themeConfig: { image: string, colorMode: object, navbar: object, footer: object, prism: object }

interface.name: Navbar Config
interface.signature: navbar: { title: string, logo: object, items: array }

interface.name: Footer Config
interface.signature: footer: { style: string, links: array, copyright: string }

interface.name: Authors YAML Schema
interface.signature: author_key: { name, title, url, image_url, page, socials: { x, linkedin, github, newsletter } }

tests.standards: Manual testing required for this configuration story. Validate by running local dev server (npm start) and inspecting rendered site. Check responsive design on multiple viewports. Verify color mode toggle works. Test navigation links. Validate metadata in HTML source.
tests.locations: No automated tests for configuration changes. Testing performed via local development server at localhost:3000 and visual inspection.

test.description: Verify site configuration includes custom title, tagline, updated navbar, footer, and color scheme

ideas.test: - Start dev server and inspect page title - Check navbar contains Blog, GitHub links - Verify footer has social/contact links - Test color mode toggle (light/dark)

test.description: Validate navigation structure with blog, docs, and GitHub links

ideas.test: - Click all navbar links, verify they navigate correctly - Test on mobile viewport (375px, 768px) - Test on desktop viewport (1024px+) - Verify hamburger menu on mobile
- Check authors.yml has James Crowley information - Verify social metadata in HTML head tags - Inspect logo/favicon (if customized) - Validate professional description
- Test mobile viewports using browser DevTools - Test desktop viewports - Toggle dark/light mode - Compare with default theme for regressions
